title: BIOLOG migration proposal
description: ADR-0005 Decision 1.1. Written by any feature agent. Carries NO sequence number - a proposal is a request to join the history, never part of it. Deliberately a different shape from migration-record.schema.json so a proposal can never be mistaken for something ready to run. Examples are SYNTHETIC.

proposal_id.description: Canonical evt_ identifier for this proposal (ADR-0001 section 1).

story_id.description: The Jira story this migration belongs to, e.g. BIO-IDN-003.

domain_conflict_group.description: The conflict group the SCHEMA CHANGE belongs to (identity, credential, biometric, ...) - never 'migration-core', which is reserved for the sequencing process itself (ADR-0005 Decision 1.1).

up.description: The forward change. Opaque to this contract - a real SQL/DDL body or an equivalent script reference.

reversibility.description: ADR-0005 Decision 3.2. Exactly one of down or (reversible:false + repair_procedure) - never neither.

forwardSafety.description: ADR-0005 Decision 3.1/3.4. A breaking change must name the earlier deprecating record its window depends on, and that record must itself declare deprecation_window - any other record at that sequence position is not a relevant dependency.

deprecation_window.description: Present only on an additive record that deliberately opens a deprecation window a later breaking record may depend on (ADR-0005 Decision 3.3). Naming the target makes the dependency relevant, not merely present.

breaks.description: Present on a breaking record: the exact target it removes, matched against the referenced record's deprecation_window.target (ADR-0005 Decision 3.5). An omitted breaks can never match a real target and is refused at assignment, the same as a wrongly-named one.

proofs.description: ADR-0005 Decision 4. Both mandatory before sequence assignment.
